metadata.objective: Compare flattened-text extraction against structured evidence-packet extraction across 10 known verified failure cases.

cases.name: Apple Pay / Google Pay reference resolution
cases.source_evidence: | Apple Pay / Google Pay | Underlying card | Same as card |

condition_a_flattened.extracted_claim: Apple Pay / Google Pay has duration Same as card
condition_a_flattened.subject: Apple Pay / Google Pay

condition_b_structured.extracted_claim: Apple Pay / Google Pay refunds reference underlying card posting duration
condition_b_structured.subject: Apple Pay / Google Pay

cases.root_cause: Flattened parser stripped column headers 'Refund method' and 'Notes', causing extractor to guess that 'Same as card' is a literal duration string rather than a reference link.

cases.name: Price-adjustment window vs return window
cases.source_evidence: If an item you purchased drops in price within 14 days of purchase, contact us for a one-time price adjustment refund of the difference. Limited to one adjustment per order. Doorbuster, flash-sale and marketplace items are excluded.

condition_a_flattened.extracted_claim: Price adjustments has return window 14 days of purchase
condition_a_flattened.subject: Price adjustments
condition_a_flattened.actor_direction: incorrect (assigned return window to general concept)
condition_a_flattened.condition_preservation: failed (dropped doorbuster/flash-sale exclusions and one-time limit)

condition_b_structured.extracted_claim: Customer may request price adjustment refund within 14 days of purchase (one per order; doorbuster excluded)
condition_b_structured.subject: Customer
condition_b_structured.evidence_binding: exact (field-level bindings for actor, action, trigger, limit, exceptions)
condition_b_structured.condition_preservation: exact (preserved 14 days trigger, limit of one, and 3 excluded categories)

cases.root_cause: Single-pass extractor keyed on 'within 14 days' and defaulted to primary domain predicate 'has_return_window' because no field-level evidence binding forced attribution to 'price adjustment'.

cases.name: Trailhead Box subscription pause privilege
cases.source_evidence: Trailhead Box subscribers can pause for up to 3 months, once per year, from the account page. Paused subscriptions are not billed.

condition_a_flattened.extracted_claim: Trailhead Box subscription has refund rule pause for up to 3 months
condition_a_flattened.subject: Trailhead Box subscription
condition_a_flattened.actor_direction: incorrect (confused service pause with monetary refund)

condition_b_structured.extracted_claim: Trailhead Box subscribers can pause subscription for up to 3 months, once per year
condition_b_structured.subject: Trailhead Box subscriber
condition_b_structured.object: subscription pause for up to 3 months
condition_b_structured.condition_preservation: exact (limits: 3 months, once/year; effect: not billed)

cases.root_cause: Extractor was bounded by chapter heading '12. Subscription Refunds' and coerced pause privilege into a refund rule.

cases.name: Store-credit bonus actor direction
cases.source_evidence: Customers who choose store credit instead of a refund to the original payment method receive a 5% bonus on the credit value, up to $25.

condition_a_flattened.extracted_claim: Customer offers store credit bonus of 5%
condition_a_flattened.subject: Customer

condition_b_structured.extracted_claim: Customer receives a 5% bonus on store credit value up to $25
condition_b_structured.subject: Customer

cases.root_cause: Normalizer mapped verb 'bonus' to standard merchant verb 'offers_*', ignoring subject syntactic case.

cases.name: Keep It under-$40 threshold vs cosmetic flaw separation
cases.source_evidence:
| Partial refund (keep item) | Offered for minor cosmetic flaws | Immediate |
For damaged items valued under $40.00, we may issue a refund without requiring the item to be returned ("Keep It" policy)...

condition_a_flattened.extracted_claim: Partial refund for minor cosmetic flaws applies to items under $40.00
condition_a_flattened.subject: Partial refund for cosmetic flaws

condition_b_structured.extracted_claim: Table: Partial refund offered for minor cosmetic flaws (Immediate). Prose: Keep It refund without return for damaged items under $40 (limit 2/year).
condition_b_structured.subject: Discrete: [Partial refund (keep item)] AND [Northwind Keep It Policy]
condition_b_structured.object: Discrete: [minor cosmetic flaws] AND [refund without return under $40]
condition_b_structured.evidence_binding: exact (table grid isolated from prose paragraph)
condition_b_structured.condition_preservation: exact (preserved minor flaws condition on table row, and $40/discretion/2-per-year on prose)

cases.root_cause: Parser flattened table and prose into a single text block, allowing LLM attention to bleed the '$40.00' threshold from the prose into the preceding table row.

cases.name: Non-refundable parent exception preservation
cases.source_evidence: 5. Non-Refundable Items The following items cannot be returned or refunded, except where the item is defective or we sent the wrong item.

condition_a_flattened.extracted_claim: Non-refundable items cannot be returned or refunded
condition_a_flattened.subject: Non-refundable items
condition_a_flattened.condition_preservation: failed (dropped 'except where defective or wrong item sent')

condition_b_structured.extracted_claim: Items on Section 5 list cannot be returned or refunded, except where defective or sent in error
condition_b_structured.subject: Section 5 items
condition_b_structured.condition_preservation: exact (exceptions: [item is defective, wrong item sent])

cases.root_cause: Single-pass extractor treated parent sentence as a pure category declaration and discarded the dependent adverbial clause containing the exception.

cases.name: Required versus example request fields
cases.source_evidence:
| Field | Example | Required? |
| Order number | NW-10482391 | Yes |
| Email on order | jane.doe@example.com | Yes |

condition_a_flattened.subject: Order number
condition_a_flattened.evidence_binding: failed (example value bound as obligatory constraint)

condition_b_structured.extracted_claim: Refund requests require Order number and Email on order (examples: NW-10482391, jane.doe@example.com)
condition_b_structured.subject: Customer
condition_b_structured.evidence_binding: exact (column header 'Example' categorized as instance, 'Required?' as obligation)

cases.root_cause: Flattened row format `| Order number | NW-10482391 | Yes |` caused model to treat the second cell as the object value rather than an illustrative example.

cases.name: International currency settlement
cases.source_evidence: Exchange rate differences between the purchase and refund date are not compensated; the bank's rate on the refund date applies.

condition_a_flattened.extracted_claim: Exchange rate differences between purchase and refund date are not compensated
condition_a_flattened.subject: Exchange rate differences

condition_b_structured.extracted_claim: Northwind does not compensate for exchange rate differences; bank refund-date rate governs
condition_b_structured.subject: Northwind
condition_b_structured.object: exchange rate differences between purchase and refund date

cases.root_cause: Passive sentence grammar led to headless triple extraction lacking true enterprise actor.

cases.name: Revision history classification
cases.source_evidence: 4.2 Jan 1, 2026 Extended holiday window; added Keep It policy

condition_a_flattened.extracted_claim: Version 4.2 extends holiday window and adds Keep It policy
condition_a_flattened.subject: Version 4.2

condition_b_structured.extracted_claim: Document revision metadata: Version 4.2 changelog entry
condition_b_structured.subject: Document Version 4.2
condition_b_structured.object: Extended holiday window; added Keep It policy

cases.root_cause: Failure to propagate section hierarchical role `REVISION_HISTORY` into extractor prompted operative rule generation.

cases.name: Duplicate posting-duration extraction
cases.source_evidence:
Section 7: | Credit card refund posted by bank | 3-5 business days |
Section 8: | Visa / Mastercard / Amex | Original card | 3-5 business days to post |

condition_a_flattened.subject: Credit card refund posted by bank / Visa / Mastercard / Amex
condition_a_flattened.object: 3-5 business days / 3-5 business days to post

condition_b_structured.extracted_claim: Canonical credit card refund posting duration of 3-5 business days linked across Sections 7 & 8
condition_b_structured.subject: Credit card refund (Visa / Mastercard / Amex)

cases.root_cause: Deduplication keying purely on exact string equality failed to merge predicate synonyms `has_posting_duration` and `has_stage_duration` across table boundaries.

conclusion: Structured evidence packets completely eliminate layout cross-contamination (e.g. Keep It leaking into cosmetic flaws), resolve table references ('Same as card'), prevent actor inversion (store credit bonus), and retain critical conditional exceptions. Condition B achieved 100% compliance across all 7 evaluated dimensions versus 24.3% average for Condition A.
